page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Local storage is provided via a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU features 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing on Geekbench and text generation for a small 135M LLM model reach top-tier status in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations on Passmark fall within the average range. Text generation for a medium 7B LLM model remains strong, though prompt processing speeds are average.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is configured for compute-heavy workloads rather than memory-intensive databases. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include text processing, image processing, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
